confidence_notes: Restaurant and coffee anchors come from aggregated cost-of-living sites (citycost, whereandwhen, nomad.watch, oysterlist, mylifeelsewhere). The sources mostly agree on budget meals (about USD 6) and cappuccino (about USD 3.3-3.7), but disagree on beer (USD 1.7-4.5). The midrange meal for two sits between the low aggregator figures and typical Korean three-course pricing. Cocktail and wine prices were not looked up directly. They are estimated from how beer prices usually compare to other drinks in Korean regional cities, where Western drinks cost noticeably more, so they are less certain. Accommodation prices were not searched. They are model estimates based on Jeonju's hanok guesthouse and hostel market, with July demand taken into account. The FX figure is the RBA 4pm rate for 2026-11-18 as reported in search results, not read directly from the RBA page.
comparable_city_reasoning: Treated as a mid-sized Korean regional city with prices a little below Seoul and Busan and similar to Daegu or Gwangju. Tourism demand around Hanok Village raises guesthouse prices slightly.
